question.text: Consider two straight lines, each of which is tangent to both the circle <math><msup><mrow><mi>x</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>+</mo><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math> and the parabola <math><msup><mrow><mi>y</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn><mi>x</mi></math> . Let these lines intersect at the point <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math>. Consider the ellipse whose center is at the origin <math><mi>O</mi><mo>(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mi> </mi><mn>0</mn><mo>)</mo></math> and whose semi-major axis is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>O</mi><mi>Q</mi></math>. If the length of the minor axis of this ellipse is <math><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></math>, then the which of the following statement(s) is (are) TRUE?

options.text: For the ellipse, the eccentricity is <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math> and the length of the latus rectum is 1

For the ellipse, the eccentricity is  <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>  and the length of the latus rectum is  <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>

The area of the region bounded by the ellipse between the lines <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math> and <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math> is <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>

The area of the region bounded by the ellipse between the lines  <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt></mrow></mfrac></math>  and  <math><mi>x</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></math>  is  <math><mfrac><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>16</mn></mrow></mfrac><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>π</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text: Let equation of common tangent is \(\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{m} \mathrm{x}+\frac{1}{\mathrm{~m}}\) \(\therefore\left|\frac{0+0+\frac{1}{\mathrm{~m}}}{\sqrt{1+\mathrm{m}^{2}}}\right|=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \Rightarrow \mathrm{m}^{4}+\mathrm{m}^{2}-2=0 \Rightarrow \mathrm{m}=\pm 1\) Equation of common tangents are \(\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{x}+1\) and \(\mathrm{y}=-\mathrm{x}+1\) point \(Q\) is \((-1,0)\) \(\therefore\) Equation of ellipse is \(\frac{x^{2}}{1}+\frac{y^{2}}{1 / 2}=1\) (A) \(\mathrm{e}=\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{2}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\) and \(\mathrm{LR}=\frac{2 \mathrm{~b}^{2}}{\mathrm{a}}=1\) (C) Area \(2 \cdot \int_{1 / \sqrt{2}}^{1} \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \cdot \sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^{2}} \mathrm{dx}=\sqrt{2}\left[\frac{\mathrm{x}}{2} \sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^{2}}+\frac{1}{2} \sin ^{-1} \mathrm{x}\right]_{1 / \sqrt{2}}^{1}\) \(=\sqrt{2}\left[\frac{\pi}{4}-\left(\frac{1}{4}+\frac{\pi}{8}\right)\right]=\sqrt{2}\left(\frac{\pi}{8}-\frac{1}{4}\right]=\frac{\pi-2}{4 \sqrt{2}}\) Correct answers are (A) and (C).
